Minimum Edges to Make Graph Strongly Connected

You are operating a planetary-wide information relay system composed of N satellite nodes and M directional laser links. A relay system is called fully operational if information can navigate from any satellite to any other satellite, following directed laser links.

Your mandate is to restructure the network with the minimum number of new directed edges to make it fully operational. Given the directed graph, compute the minimum number of edges to add to ensure every satellite can reach every other satellite.
explanation: We first decompose the directed graph into its Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) using Kosaraju's Algorithm (two-pass DFS). Each SCC can be treated as a single super-node, creating a Condensation DAG. On this DAG, any SCC with in-degree 0 needs an inbound edge, and any SCC with out-degree 0 needs an outbound edge. The answer is max(count of SCCs with in-degree 0, count of SCCs with out-degree 0). A special case: if there is exactly 1 SCC, the graph is already strongly connected and the answer is 0.
